articles.body:
The Fallen follows immediately after defeating Alduin for the first time in Alduin's Bane , and is the fourteenth main quest in Skyrim . With Alduin having escaped after your tussle, you now have to track down one of his allies to find out what he's doing next.

Get Greybeards' help in negotiating a truce

Learn the Call Dragon shout to summon Odahviing

Paarthurnax, Arngeir, or Esbern reveal that Dragonsreach in Whiterun was originally built to hold other dragons. The plan is to capture one of Alduin's ilk and convince the captive to betray Alduin. Before that happens, however, you will need to convince Jarl of Whiterun first.

While Jarl Balgruuf (or whoever is in his place following the events of the Civil War ) fully comprehends the threat of the World-Eater looming over him like a dark shadow, an even greater threat - the clash between the Stormcloaks and Imperial Legion - perturbs him even more.

If you have not already done some of the Civil War quests , the quest Season Unending will now begin, during which you are to negotiate a peace council to help suspend the civil strife while the dragons are taken cared of. You will have to complete Season Unending (or pick a side) before you can continue with The Fallen.

Conversely, if you've already picked a side and captured nine Holds, then the jarl will let you proceed with The Fallen right away.

Learn the Call Dragon shout from Paarthurnax (if you had already picked a side in the Civil War) or Esbern. The latter will also give you the quest to slay Paarthurnax for his past crimes on humanity. Note that this is optional. Killing Paarthurnax will, understandably, upset Arngeir. However, he will still arrange the negotiations you need to complete The Fallen.

Using Call Dragon at the end of the balcony will call Odahviing to the area. As the dragon enters Dragonsreach, he will pick up the guard, leaving just the sword and torch behind.

From here this quest is really simple. Whenever you get the chance, hit the dragon with Dragonrend and run inside the large opening. The dragon will land on the balcony and follow you in and be captured by the trap waiting above.

Speak to Odahviing to negotiate an agreement to help each other. He'll explain that Alduin has gone to Skuldafn Temple, and will even agree to take you there if you release him.

When you are ready to go, talk to the nearby guard upstairs to free Odahviing, who you can now talk to and travel to Skuldafn Temple, starting The World-Eater's Eyrie quest.

articles.title: Alien Planet Biome Guide - Steal An Egg [Roblox] Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Alien Planet is a specific biome that you can reach while playing Steal an Egg. There are several unique gameplay aspects to this area, along with several
articles.body:
The Alien Planet is a specific biome that you can reach while playing Steal an Egg . There are several unique gameplay aspects to this area, along with several notable new pets that you can unlock by stealing the eggs from the biome 's Guardian. In this guide, we'll be breaking down everything you need to know about the Alien Planet biome and how it all works in Steal an Egg.

Here's everything centered around the Alien Planet biome.

You can access this area by having at least 250b speed on your character. Although you can still visit this area if you are below this speed, if you are trying to steal eggs from the Guardian of this zone, they will easily catch you. Meeting or exceeding this speed limit is the best way to collect the various eggs and pets from this zone.

These are all of the unique pets that you can get from the Alien Planet zone. There are standard eggs and pets that you can get, and then there are some that exclusively appear during a Flooded Alien Planet event. The Flooded Alien Planet occurs during a Tidal Surge event, where the entire biome is underwater.

A Flooded Alien Planet can occur following a Tidal Surge.

The Tidal Surge event has a chance to happen at night, flooding the entire Alien Planet biome, giving you the chance to collect these exclusive pets that can spawn during this time.

The Alien Ferryman is an NPC you can find in the Alien Planet biome. You can speak with them, so long as you have the 250b requirement for the zone. If you do, the Alien Ferryman will give you a fishing rod and ask you to fish up to 20 different items. You can do this from the waterfall area of the Alien Planet. After you do this, they open up the Lagoon, allowing you to fish from this location as much as you want without interruption. You can even remain here between the day and night cycles and not return to your base.

Cosmic Eclipse Event and Nebuloth Kraken

The Cosmic Eclipse event is a server-wide event that occurs for five minutes. It happens every hour on the :55 and :25 minute marks. Everyone receives a notification when this happens, allowing players to potentially catch the Nebuloth Kraken from the Lagoon. You can be outside of the Lagoon when this even takes place, but I recommend being in it.

If you're in the Legoon, you have a higher chance to catch the Nebuloth Kraken. There are only 750 Nebuloth Krakens available during the event, and this counts for all servers in Steal an Egg. If 750 players catch those Krakens, those creatures disappear, and you'll need to wait until the next Cosmic Eclipse event starts to try again.

Void Pearls are a rare currency that you can get from the Alien Planet biome. There's a chance that whenever you're fishing, you might reel in Void Pearls as a reward, rather than the eggs, relics, or mutations that you can get. Alternatively, you can get Void Pearls from the Fishing Milestones page. Every fish that you catch counts as a point, and there are Void Pearl rewards for certain amounts that you reach, providing you a large amount.

You can speak with the Alien Ferryman to exchange those Void Pearls for Dark Matter mutations, which you can place on your eggs. You need at least 1,750 Void Pearls for one Dark Matter mutation.

articles.body:
Settlements are smaller areas within districts, where multiple citizens can live together in Rob Run . You can rent out settlements to other players, which will earn you passive income through a small tax on their property. In this guide, we're going to break down everything you need to do to buy a Settlement in Rob Run .

You need to purchase the Settlement Title from the Black Market before you can get a Settlement. The unlock will cost you $100,000.

After you unlock it, the price of actually purchasing the Settlement Title is $200,000, meaning you need to have at least a total of $300,000 to get a Settlement Level 1 and start renting to players.

You'll collect taxes based on resident's financial actions while they live there. If you don't have anyone living there, though, no income goes to you. You can have random players join, or friends who are trying to work with you, to boost everyone's wealth.

articles.title: Dragon Age Fans Save One of the Series' Most Beloved Features
articles.summary: Dragon Age fans have saved one of the series’ most beloved features: being able to import your world states in each game.
articles.body:
Dragon Age fans have saved one of the series’ most beloved features: being able to import your world states in each game.

With the Mass Effect trilogy, this was simple: just play through the series on the same console, and your saves are automatically carried over. The same was true going from Dragon Age: Origins into Dragon Age 2. But by the time Dragon Age: Inquisition rolled around in 2014, a new console generation was upon us, so BioWare had to get creative.

This is when we get the Dragon Age Keep . This website connects to your EA account and keeps track of all the decisions you made in the previous games. Or, you can just input whatever decisions you want manually. You can then import this crafted world state into Dragon Age: Inquisition and see your previous choices reflected in the game.

I am sure many of you can already see the problem with this system: it’s an online service that needs to be maintained. True enough, the Dragon Age Keep experiences fairly frequent outages, during which time no one can start a new Inquisition run with their choices carried over.

Now that EA has shut down BioWare , it’s unclear what will happen if the Keep goes offline again, or how long EA plans to keep it going. Thankfully, fans already have a solution, at least if you’re on PC. A couple of modders have released user-friendly ways to adjust the game files so your choices still carry over, even if EA pulls the plug on the Dragon Age Keep.

First up, there’s Thedas World State Studio - Dragon Age Keep Utility by Nexus Mods user anshela. This gives you an offline alternative to the Keep, letting you input your choices in the same tapestry format you would in the online version.

This is much more user-friendly than previous methods of editing your world state on PC. As anyone who has tried will tell you, modding Inquisition is a nightmare thanks to the Frostbite engine, but this tool should make it much more accessible.

The modder says they were already working on this before the BioWare news hit, and the fact that it is ready now is just “good/bad timing." Indeed it is, because the next Dragon Age Keep outage could be the last.

Right now, the mod files have been “quarantined” while Nexus approves the latest version, so it can’t be downloaded just yet. But once it’s up and running again, it should work just fine, judging from the response from users so far.

This isn’t the only mod you’ll need if the servers go offline. The closest thing Inquisition has to New Game Plus lets you port almost all of your unlocks into future playthroughs, but for whatever reason, this also requires the Keep to be up, even though it’s only dealing with things you’ve unlocked in Inquisition.

That is where Thedas Chronicle - World State and Golden Nug Fix by TP1231 has us covered. This will let you access the Golden Nug statue that activates item transfers even if the servers are down. As the name suggests, it will also let you play with your imported world state when the Keep is offline, but you will still need the world state that you made while the servers are up.

While it’s great to see fans get these solutions out before EA potentially pulls the plug, it is no wonder that BioWare didn’t want to risk this happening ever again. Instead, Dragon Age: The Veilguard had us input previous choices in the game itself, so it could be played offline. Granted, we had far fewer options to carry over that time around, much to the frustration of fans, but at least it means we won’t have to go through this again.

In the meantime, BioWare fans are currently fighting to save the studio’s IPs. Most notably, the Save Mass Effect movement has amassed thousands of supporters, as they urge EA to do something with the IP, rather than let the series die.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

articles.title: GTA 6 Has a Whole Animated TV Series You Can Watch In-Game
articles.summary: In yet further evidence of the lengths Rockstar has gone to in order to pack GTA 6 to the brim with content, we have our first look at an animated TV series you can watch in-game.
articles.body:
In yet further evidence of the lengths Rockstar has gone to in order to pack GTA 6 to the brim with content, we have our first look at an animated TV series you can watch in-game.

The DiscussingFilm X / Twitter account posted a teaser for Macca & Friends, a cartoon Rockstar created for GTA 6’s Weazel television network, which is also found in both the 3D Universe and HD Universe of the Grand Theft Auto series.

Exclusive first look at ‘MACCA & FRIENDS’. The series follows the adventures of Macca the Gator and his wetland friends across the state of Leonida. Coming November 19 on WEAZEL. — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) November 13, 2026

Exclusive first look at ‘MACCA & FRIENDS’. The series follows the adventures of Macca the Gator and his wetland friends across the state of Leonida. Coming November 19 on WEAZEL.

Macca & Friends has big Adult Swim vibes. It stars Pinche, a crab landlord who is going to kick out Macca the alligator if he doesn’t pay rent. There’s a talking sun, lots of other talking animals, and a police station. “The series follows the adventures of Macca the Gator and his wetland friends across the state of Leonida,” reads the description.

Reaction is a mix of disbelief that GTA 6 has an entire cartoon in the game itself to watch, and growing hype ahead of its November 19 release date. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recently told The New York Times that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game back in February. He noted that playthrough included the main story and some "optional goals with narrative ramifications," so it's unclear if he sat down to watch some in-game telly. Still, that is a sizable length regardless. For comparison, GTA 4 and 5 are around 30 hours long, while Red Dead Redemption 2 is around 50-60 hours. So, that means GTA 6 will be the longest of Rockstar's games to date.

Indeed, an in-game TV series is exactly the kind of thing fans have come to expect from Rockstar, which operates on another level to most, if not all triple-A video game companies. We know GTA 6 did not cost more than $1.5 billion to make , but it is considered to be the most expensive video game of all time.

Rockstar has insisted GTA 6 did not cost more than $1.5 billion to make, countering an online rumor, but it’s still probably the most expensive video game of all time. A recent Bloomberg report confirmed that Rockstar Games now has 4,711 staff across 12 offices, up from the 2,441 staff it had when Red Dead Redemption 2 came out in 2018. The company has doubled in size over the last eight years, which will have increased costs significantly. But it also means Rockstar is able to do things like this cartoon, which for many fans won’t be of interest, but for some will be a fun distraction.

Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier said in a video accompaniment to his making of GTA 6 article that Rockstar told him of a scripted system in the game that makes dual protagonists Jason and Lucia — or, it sounds like, any character in the game — exert different amounts of sweat depending on how much effort they’re putting into whatever activity they’re doing. Indeed, Rockstar set up a new studio in Los Angeles packed with writers, producers, and directors, just to make NPCs.

articles.title: Curt Pires and Ryan Quackenbush Announce Sci-Fi Graphic Novel Content
articles.summary: IGN can exclusively reveal a new preview of the Image Comics graphic novel Content, which spoofs our current climate of mindless content consumption and rampant AI use.
articles.body:
Curt Pires has built up a huge fan following in the comic book scene for his inventive work on books like the Star Wars/Tarantino mash-up Galactic and the Pokémon-spoofing Creature Corps . Pires is now teaming with artist Ryan Quackenbush (Junior Baker the Righteous Faker) for a new Image Comics graphic novel called Content, and it's a book that's perfect for our current age of mindless content consumption and rampant AI use.

IGN can exclusively reveal a new preview of Content. Check it out in the slideshow gallery below, but beware of some NSFW language:

Image Comics' Content: Exclusive Graphic Novel Preview

Here's Image's official summary of Content:

Fan-favorite creators Curt Pires (Creature Corps, Fireborn) and Ryan Quackenbush (Junior Baker the Righteous Faker) will team up for an all-new, original graphic novel titled, Content.

Inspired by Pires’ own time in the Hollywood dream factory, Content is set in the age of the infinite scroll. The perfect read for fans of Severance, Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, and The Social Network.

In a near-future ruled by streaming services, Trip Cruise is the most valuable mind in entertainment and the visionary architect behind the world’s biggest platform: Content. But when an experimental AI helmet meant to extract stories straight from his brain malfunctions, Trip becomes trapped inside the system he built: forced to navigate an endless hellscape of shows and fragmented memories.

His only shot at escape? Margot, his junior programmer and the only person with a strong enough human to him to take a shot at saving him. Together they’ll have to outsmart the machine designed to replace them or risk getting permanently deleted from existence.

Content will be released in comic shops on February 17 and in bookstores on March 16. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

Also hitting stores in February 2027 are Batman: Reign of Assassins and a new Sabrina the Teenage Witch storyline .

articles.title: God of War Sons of Sparta Coming to PS4 Next Week With New Content
articles.summary: Sony has revealed that God of War Sons of Sparta is coming to PS4 next week, and it's bringing two new modes with it.
articles.body:
Sony has revealed that God of War Sons of Sparta is coming to PS4 next week, and it's bringing two new modes with it.

The unexpected update for this year's action platformer prequel was announced in a PlayStation.Blog post today. In it, Sony confirmed plans to bring Kratos' earliest adventure to the last-gen console starting midnight local time November 16.

It's more than a surprise bonus platform, too, as developer Mega Cat Studios has promised two new modes that will be available on both PS4 and PS5: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. The former is described as a "race against the clock" that features speedrunning tools like a split-based timer and a persistent scoreboard. The latter is a one-hit-kill mode that affects both Kratos and his enemies.

Sony and Mega Cat tell God of War Sons of Sparta players that they'll be able to select their mode when starting a new game and selecting a save slot. Game modes can't be changed once selected. Hermes Mode, specifically, is activated only after beating the game once through and after players input the following code: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad. It's unclear if unlocking Erebus Mode has a similar old-school cheat code-esque requirement.

God of War Sons of Sparta takes one of PlayStation's most popular exclusive franchises and scales it down to let players control Kratos at a much, much earlier point in his life in ancient Greece. Shadow-dropped back in February of this year as an experimental chapter of the story for PS5, its story returns to an era fans have longed for with original Kratos actor Terrence 'T.C. Carson back in the booth.

"Every legend has a beginning – before he was a God, before he was a father, Kratos was a young Spartan!" an official story description said. "Experience an untold chapter in Kratos’ journey set during the harsh years of Spartan training alongside his brother Deimos. Through endless trials, their minds, bodies, and hearts have been molded to become Spartan soldiers for whom duty and honor mean everything. After a fellow cadet goes missing, Kratos and Deimos vow to find him and embark on an adventure that will put their training and Spartan spirit to the test."

God of War 20th Anniversary DualSense PS5 Controller

God of War Sons of Sparta was unable to generate the same level of hype the series' more recent entries have been known for. Despite the surprise of getting a new God of War game without any of the build-up, the prequel side-scroller generally received middling reviews from critics and fans. IGN gave it a 6/10 , calling it "a pretty mediocre Metroidvania" that failed "to meet the high bar set by the titans of the genre."

Franchise creator David Jaffe was less than impressed with God of War Sons of Sparta when it launched. In a video posted at the time, he said a 2.5D God of War game is "the kind of game I've always wanted" but ultimately said it was an experience he did not like and did not recommend. He even went as far as to say, "This is not God of War."

"I wanted to make a video more about what are they thinking, like what the f*** were they thinking?" Jaffe explained. "It's not a bad game by any means, it's fine, it controls decently... but to me the more fascinating part of this is, why is this in existence? I don't understand."

Like it or not, God of War Sons of Sparta offered a stopgap for Sony as it chipped away at the series' next major new entry: God of War Laufey . The PS5-exclusive title is currently set to launch May 20, 2027, following a recent delay . At least the prequel is now available for PS4 users to enjoy while they wait an extra few months.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: How to Get a Drill and Rob the Bank Vault - Rob Run Guide - IGN
articles.summary: If you're willing to take the risk,  you can raid the Looty Bay Bank on the northeast part of town in Rob Run, but it's tricky to pull off -
articles.body:
If you're willing to take the risk, you can raid the Looty Bay Bank on the northeast part of town in Rob Run , but it's tricky to pull off - you'll need to do it with a party, and you'll be fighting off multiple players who will try and stop you. Before you can even attempt it, there's specific gear that you'll need to get and bring with you. In this guide, we'll be walking you through everything you need to know about how to rob the bank in Rob Run.

You'll need a certain amount of gear if you want to gain access to the Looty Bay Bank Vault. You can't merely walk in.

You need a standard Dril l at the bare minimum. Having mini drills is also useful to open the smaller safes within the Bank Vault. If you want to unlock everything in the Bank Vault, you also need the ID Card , which unlocks the Gold Deposit room. However, the ID Card is not required to access the Bank Vault, but it allows you to collect a large quantity of gold.

The Drill is available at Lenny's Motel . Head inside the building, and make your way over to the Suspicious Door. Here, you'll be able to exchange some of the items you've collected while playing Rob Run. For the Drill, you need an Epic Action Camera , two USB Hacking Tools , and $50,000. This will give you access to the Drill.

Although not required, if you want to get as much loot as possible, the ID Card gives you access to the Bank Vault's gold vault. There's a bunch of gold there that you can sell for a solid amount of money.

The ID Card can also be obtained at the Suspicious Door at Lenny's Motel. There, you can exchange at least one Deposit Box Key for an ID Card.

Finally, you'll need Mini Drills. The Mini Drills are what you're going to use to unlock the larger safes once your inside. There are three safes that you can use these on inside of the bank vault.

When you have all of those items (or at least the Drill and Mini Drills), head over to the Looty Bay Bank on the northeast side of the map. You can enter through the front entrance, where you can explore much of the bank's first and second floors. Your primary goal is to reach the bottom floor, behind the teller's counter, where you'll find the vault.

The person who has the Drill won't be able to use it until they've changed their status to Criminal. When this happens, expect many of the alarms and sirens to begin going off as there are cameras on the first floor. You'll want to place the drill on the vault door immediately, as it takes one minute for the drill to punch through the vault.

After the drill breaks through, you have free reign of the vault and can begin looting. You'll find money on the central counter, a trio of vaults you can use the mini drills on the left side of the room, and several safety deposit boxes you can open on the right side. In the back of the room is the gold room, which you can only access if you have the ID Card.

Although you can grab as much as you want, expect nearly every player Cop on the server to know what's happening and speed over to you.

articles.title: Marvel Confirms the Avengers Team Lineup That Anthony Mackie's Captain America Will Lead in Doomsday
articles.summary: Marvel has confirmed the lineup of heroes that Anthony Mackie's Captain America will lead into battle when Avengers: Doomsday premieres next month.
articles.body:
Marvel has confirmed the lineup of heroes that Anthony Mackie's Captain America will lead into battle when Avengers: Doomsday premieres next month.

Which portion of the big team-up movie's ensemble cast will fall specifically into the Avengers camp was confirmed by Empire . During an interview with some of the movie's cast and crew, the minds behind the Marvel Cinematic Universe talked about what each hero is bringing into the fight and which camp they have ultimately fallen into.

With so many different teams from across the MCU multiverse to keep track of, you may have been a bit confused about who was fighting who and which superpowered being was on whose side. For Mackie, returning as Captain America means leading a new team, and that team now officially encompasses him, Falcon (Danny Ramirez), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Thor (Chris Hemsworth), and Shang-Chi (Simu Liu).

Hot Toys' Avengers: Doomsday Figures - Image Gallery

The full team includes faces new and old as Earth's Mightiest Heroes band together to fight off Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. It'll be far from Mackie's first rodeo as Sam Wilson, but donning the Captain America mantle represents a completely new moment not only for himself but for the characters he's leading. He opened up about the role change during the interview.

"In Endgame , Steve gave him the shield and says, 'You need to be the leader of the Avengers,'" he said. "Now you get to see more of him leading the charge with everyone into battle."

Although we know little about what exactly Doctor Doom's master plan entails, we do know that the primary Avengers team will have some help. Classic X-Men characters and the recently established Fantastic Four will be there to help, too, as will the motley crew of half-heroes known as the New Avengers. The group will almost certainly clash with the classic Avengers lineup, with wild cards like Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) sure to throw a wrench into things , too.

There's… a lot going on in the MCU, but Avengers: Doomsday will give everyone a chance to get their act together. Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige also explained what kind of team viewers can expect.

"We're coming out of years of seemingly no organized Avengers team, and that's exactly when they face these incursions," he said, referencing a post-credits scene from the recently released Avengers: Endgame Encore . "That’s always fun, to put your heroes on the back foot."

Avengers: Doomsday is set to premiere December 18, 2026, meaning we're only a little more than a month away from its release date. Despite there being so little time left, Marvel has shared quite a bit about the project in the lead-up to its launch. Just yesterday, we learned that Deadpool and Wolverine stars Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds have writing credits on the movie . Feige also debunked one of the biggest theories regarding potential connections between Downey's Tony Stark and Doctor Doom .

articles.title: Crazy Taxi: World Tour Final Map Revealed
articles.summary: The next map confirmed for Crazy Taxi: World Tour is India, boasting three different zones that celebrate the country’s many cultures and hallmarks — and yes, Bollywood films make an appearance.
articles.body:
The next map confirmed for Crazy Taxi: World Tour is India, boasting three different zones that celebrate the country’s many cultures and hallmarks — and yes, Bollywood films make an appearance.

Crazy Taxi: World Tour will boast five international maps: the US West Coast, Germany, Japan, Brazil, and finally, India. The India map will feature three distinct zones, labeled City, Countryside, and Industrial.

The City zone is all hustle and bustle, with vibrant marketplaces, nightlife, and architecture. The Country zone is where you can find ancient temples and zoom through the natural landscape, while the Industrial zone takes players on a tour of its trade and commerce hubs, as well as a look at one of the world’s oldest trains.

The game’s official trailer for the India map even teases that players might find themselves on the “set of a Bollywood film,” showing a passenger holding a camera who appears to be a movie director.

This is the latest news to come from this highly-anticipated installment in Sega’s beloved arcade racing game after a closed beta test gave fans a hint at what its multiplayer mode might look like. A signup website for the test says players could participate in two different modes: Pickup Race and Cops ‘N’ Cabbies.

In the Pickup Race mode, up to 6 players compete to drop off as many passengers as possible within a specific time limit and earn as much cash as they can. In Cops ‘N’ Cabbies, two teams of players face off against each other, with one being cabbies and the other being cops hot on their trail.

In addition to multiplayer, the game also has a story mode that follows its main character, Axel, as he chases a gang of international car thieves across the globe to recover his stolen ride, bussing passengers across each country along the way.

We got the chance to preview Crazy Taxi: World Tour back in August. IGN’s Scott White praised the game for its “simple-yet-exciting sort of fun that arcade games excel at, that makes you want to just keep playing,” calling it an “almost refreshingly uncomplicated palette cleanser free of skill trees, crafting systems, and the other chaff that seems to be in every game you play nowadays.”

Crazy Taxi: World Tour launches in early 2027 on Xbox X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and PC.

articles.title: The Lenovo Legion Pro 7i Combines Gaming, Versatility, and Portability in One Premium Package
articles.body:
In our increasingly digital era, what we require from our laptops has expanded exponentially. Gone are the days of only caring about how well they run games and Microsoft Office. Now we also need them for content creation, our jobs, schoolwork, and with a design you can take on the go.

The Lenovo Legion Pro 7i addresses all those needs, providing the versatility and flexibility to shift between tasks seamlessly while also having the power to deliver a high-end gaming experience.

We’re unabashed gamers at IGN, so gaming performance is always going to be a major focus for us with laptops. The Lenovo Legion Pro 7i delivers in that regard, thanks to Intel Core Ultra 9 processors that enable high peak performance. Combined with its full-speed 2.5G ethernet and HDMI 2.1, it performs more like a desktop.

It also has the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series graphics card, either the 5070, 5080, or 5090. The latter two options provide a full 175W of power, which really unlocks the elite performance of the machine. The gaming experience is completed by a gorgeous 16-inch OLED display with 16:10 aspect ratio, 240 Hz refresh rate, and wide color gamut. It uses Lenovo PureSight to maintain crystal clear image quality and smooth motion. Put simply, if you’re looking for top-of-the-line gaming, this has it.

All of this is supported by the Legion AI Engine+, which dynamically optimizes system performance in real time. It can shift power distribution and balance the loads of the GPU and CPU to optimize the system for the most demanding games, as well as help with heat management. That’s also aided by the Legion ColdFront cooling system, which improves airflow and allows for more efficient heat dissipation to keep performance stable.

While gaming is obviously important to us, we recognize that a laptop’s value in 2026 is reliant on it being capable of handling much more than that. Luckily, the Lenovo Legion Pro 7i shines there too.

For the content creators out there, it can easily handle photo and video editing, streaming, graphic design, and professional workloads. The Legion AI Engine+ system also helps with this, since it can tune software to account for what you’re currently working on. That means performance stays strong even during intensive tasks like video rendering or 3D modeling. And its ultra-fast SSD storage means you can quickly switch apps and load files in seconds.

This is all contained within a machine that doesn’t skimp on aesthetics. It has a sleek design made with premium materials and an aluminum finish that gives it a professional look. It won’t look out of place at a coffee shop, but its customizable RGB lighting also gives you options for a little fun.

The Lenovo Legion Pro 7i weighs in at a bit under 6 pounds, so it has some heft to it but is still lightweight enough to be easily transportable. And considering all the bells and whistles it manages to pack in, the weight coming in that low is impressive.

All in all, it proves to be an incredibly powerful machine capable of handling just about anything you throw at it. To learn more about the Lenovo Legion Pro 7i, including all its tech specs and port information, you can check it out on Lenovo’s website . And for more coverage of the best tech out there, stay tuned to IGN.

articles.body:
Wizards of the Coast is hosting a preview panel at MagicCon Atlanta, showing off all the sets coming to Magic in 2027. While we know of most of the in-universe sets coming to the game next year, the real mystery is the two yet-to-be revealed Universes Beyond crossover sets.

Unfortunately, WotC didn't spend any time showing off the next Universes Beyond sets, and just focused on Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, the first set that will be coming out February 5, 2027.

Preorders are now up on Amazon for the new set , and there was a fun little segment with puppets and Brian Henson, so that helped a little bit.

I was watching the event live, and you can scroll below to see the event as it happened.

Magic: The Gathering – Nauctis: The Sunken Realm New Cards

As of right now, you can get Squenn and Cragg stickers on Magic Arena.

Apparently that's the show. So it was just Nauctis. There was no information about the two Universes Beyond sets that are yet to be released, and they only showed a few cards from the first set next year.

They just opened the curtains to reveal four puppeteers, which are needed to puppet the two characters. Apparently they're very complicated, and there's also two other people who are voicing the characters.

Brian Henson has come on stage to talk more about the creation of Squen and Cragg.

Henson is giving Wizards of the Coast props for being the #1 employer of painters in the world, and is also talking about the creation of the puppets that just took over the last segment.

They're rolling a clip. And it even has a musical number.

Now two puppets have taken the stage for the "Squen and Cragg Show" to kick off the next chapter of the preview event.

They weren't able to show off much more information about the show, but I definitely can't wait to watch it myself. The art looks incredible.

It sounds like the Magic show isn't going to just focus on one world, but rather a whole collection of different planes, which is true to the card game. It's called "Magic the Gathering: Planeswalker" and it's coming out in 2027.

The Magic show will be animated and it's going to be about some of the Planeswalkers. "What we have to go off of is thousands of worlds" "It's not just world-building, it's worlds-building."

Here it is, the series! We've known there's been a Magic The Gathering Show coming for a while, and now we're going to hear more.

There will also be a Planeswalker Encyclopedia coming out in September 2027.

The Legend of Zelda games are filled with puzzles for Link to solve. Now there’s a Zelda-themed puzzle for you to solve outside of the games, in real life. It’s a cast metal Triforce, like you’d find in most Zelda games, but it’s a brain teaser. The goal is to figure out how to take it apart, and then figure out how to put it back together. articles.title: Darth Vader's Actual Lightsaber Just Sold for $4.875 Million, Breaking Star Wars Auction Records
articles.summary: A Star Wars auction has just broken records, as Darth Vader's prop lightsaber from the original trilogy sells for almost $5 million.
articles.body:
A prop lightsaber wielded by Darth Vader in the original Star Wars trilogy has just sold at auction for almost $5 million.

This is the most amount of money a Star Wars prop has ever sold for, and it’s easy to see why. The lightsaber was featured in The Empire Strikes Back — largely seen as the best of the bunch — and Return of the Jedi , making it at least 46 years old.

As reported by The Guardian , the sale was done through Heritage Auctions , and sold for $4.875 million. The eye-watering figure beat the previous overall record of $3,875,000, which Heritage achieved with Tom Jung’s original half-sheet key poster painting for Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope. It also eclipsed the previous record for a screen-used Star Wars prop: Heritage’s $3,750,000 sale of Luke Skywalker’s lightsaber and severed hand effects rig on July 15, 2026.

"Vader’s lightsaber is an artifact from the very heart of the saga, and its result led a historic auction," Joe Maddalena, Heritage’s Executive Vice President, said.

The item description gives us some more details on the prop itself. For instance, this is the version that was used when the lightsabers were “ignited," so there are “mounting bolts” that would have been used to attach a wooden blade, later edited to look like a lightsaber. Because of this, we know it would have been used by both David Prowse (the guy usually in the Darth Vader suit) and Bob Anderson, who handled fight scenes and stunts.

In other words, yes, this is the lightsaber that was on-screen during the fight on Bespin between Vader and Luke.

How Much Every Star Wars Movie Made Opening Weekend

The Game Awards is coming to Roblox for the first time this December, giving fans another way to watch Geoff Keighley's annual gaming shindig, complete with live voting, virtual merchandise, and the opportunity to experience the whole thing alongside other players.

The Game Awards 2026 will stream live on Roblox starting Thursday, December 10, marking the first time an external awards show has been livestreamed on the platform. articles.title: Robert Pattinson’s James Bond Deal Offers Higher Pay for Fewer Films Than Rivals
articles.summary: Purported details of Robert Pattinson’s screen test deal to audition for James Bond 26 have come to light, and they reveal that he’s being treated differently than the four other actors in contention.
articles.body:
Purported details of Robert Pattinson’s screen test deal to audition for James Bond 26 have come to light, and they reveal that he’s being treated differently than the four other actors in contention.

According to Puck’s Matthew Belloni , as part of auditioning for the role of 007, the five actors on the shortlist – Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor , Nicholas Hoult and Pattinson – all had to sign contracts agreeing to be in Bond 26 plus options for subsequent sequels. That’s all standard procedure on Bond films, including when Daniel Craig auditioned for Casino Royale.

At 40, Pattinson is not just the oldest of the actors vying for 007 but also the biggest star (and, thus, the most expensive choice).

Citing three sources familiar with the dealmaking on Bond 26, “O’Connor and Lowden, for instance, were required to sign up for four Bonds, if chosen. Pattinson, on the other hand, was able to lower that commitment to three (plus a whole lot more money than the others), given his stardom. So whoever is chosen will confer upon Amazon MGM different rights to their services. That’s only a problem in success, of course, and I doubt, given the stakes here, that the filmmakers would choose their Bond based on who’s cheaper. But unlike with previous installments, it suggests the studio is willing or even eager to sacrifice a bit to get a ‘name’ star to front its most important franchise.”

Puck claims Pattinson and Hoult screen-tested after the other three actors did, which might suggest Amazon MGM, producers David Heyman and Amy Pascal, and director Denis Villeneuve weren’t entirely happy with the tests from the lesser known actors.

While past James Bond actors have largely been unknown (Roger Moore and Pierce Brosnan were TV stars), the speculation is that the 60+ year-old franchise could use a boost from a known actor who appeals to younger audiences and would thus minimize commercial risks for the studio.

“Pattinson’s test deal was so difficult to close, per two sources familiar with the process, that some involved were left wondering why the filmmakers would bother if they didn’t really [their emphasis] want him,” Belloni writes.

“Honestly, my biggest surprise when I heard he had tested for Bond casting director Nina Gold was that he’d agreed to test at all. Pattinson already has a pretty well-known body of work, he’s familiar to Villeneuve, and he basically played a version of Bond in Nolan’s Tenet. He seems well above having to test. But Pattinson did test… suggesting he [their emphasis] really wants it, too.”

All signs point to the official announcement of the next James Bond star before the end of the year, which dovetails nicely with the release of Denis Villeneuve’s new film with Robert Pattinson, Dune: Part Three .

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Rainbow Six: Vegas Reportedly Returning With New Installment
articles.summary: Ubisoft has reportedly given a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas series the green light and a codename.
articles.body:
Ubisoft has reportedly given a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas series the green light and a codename.

Details on a long-awaited (and unexpected) return to a fan-favorite corner of the Rainbow Six universe come from an Insider Gaming report. The publisher is said to have given its Ubisoft Montreal team the go-ahead to begin work on a new Vegas installment, with two other projects reportedly also in the works there.

Rainbow Six: Vegas started with the release of the original game in 2006 before it returned for a sequel in 2008. Whether the new game will be called Rainbow Six: Vegas 3 or something else is unclear, though the site's sources say it's expected to be more like the former rather than something like a remake. It also stated that it's being worked on with the apt codename, "Spades."

That's just one of the three games the Montreal studio is reportedly working on. The report wasn't able to confirm much about the remaining projects but said one source suggested at least one other game is planned to take place in the Rainbow Six universe in some capacity.

The Rainbow Six franchise as a whole existed long before popular entries like Rainbow Six Siege or even the Vegas series. Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six traces all the way back to the late '90s but has splintered into a wide variety of gameplay experiences and offerings. Siege is no doubt the most well-known iteration today thanks to how Ubisoft has supported its tactical gameplay since its 2015 launch, but the most recent entry actually arrived in 2022 with Rainbow Six Extraction .

Despite nearly 20 years passing since the last Vegas game, it's remained a beloved corner of the universe for many. IGN gave the original game a 7.6/10 when it launched for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. We then gave the sequel's limited edition release an 8.4/10 .

Ubisoft seems to be still in the early stages of its unannounced Rainbow Six: Vegas continuation, so don't expect to see it launch for at least a few more years. While that may mean we'll have passed the 20-year mark since the last game, we hopefully won't have to wait quite as long to learn more about it. Until then, it's best to keep expectations low while the publisher keeps its cards close to its chest.

Meanwhile, we do know about a few other projects Ubisoft has up its sleeve. Rainbow Six Tactics , for example, was announced in August and will launch sometime next year. A Splinter Cell remake is also in the works, even if it's been a while since we heard from it .

articles.title: Netflix's Heartland Gives Jessica Chastain a Chance to Deliver a Solid Performance in a Middling Mystery
articles.summary: Netflix's Heartland review: Jessica Chastain locks in for a country music mystery that unfolds on autopilot.
articles.body:
A former country rock star searches for her missing niece in Shana Feste’s Heartland, a film with the broad appearance of a neo-noir, but one that doesn’t have nearly enough thrills or intrigue. The story comes from a place of love, both for country music and for Nashville. However, it unfolds too mechanically to unearth the seedy underbelly at which it hints, making for lackluster mystery despite Jessica Chastain’s enormous efforts at drawing emotions from a tepid script.

It begins interestingly enough, with Chastain’s washed-up, tough-as-nails musician Misty Jones huddled over a grave as she tearfully buries her dog before threatening the neighbor who killed it. None of this has any bearing on the larger plot, but it paints Misty as a cornered animal; she has nothing and no one. Her fridge is scant except for a forgotten Grammy she stores there for safe-keeping, a fun bit of environmental storytelling by way of visual information. Before long, though, this becomes the movie’s default lingua franca, with an unending number of shots of photographs and documents to try and piece together a whodunnit when Misty’s niece — the daughter of her estranged brother, an up-and-coming country artist named Charlie Heart (Carter Faith) — turns up missing.

This draws Misty back to the Nashville music scene, where she navigates ineffectual cops and seedy industry figures while retracing Charlie’s steps. The mystery of her disappearance runs parallel to Misty reacquainting herself with her problem-child past and through predatory people and places she once knew, leading to an eventual overlap of these simultaneous threads by way of a family secret. However, each time Heartland features a major reveal, it zips forward far too quickly alongside its umpteenth country music cue, as though it were entering some well-established final act.

In the process, what you’re left with is a story where Misty stumbles her way into information or ping-pongs between various characters — like Garett Hedlund’s charismatic producer Roy Combs — and ends up feeling like an inactive protagonist despite technically driving the plot. She moves from place to place, but rare are the moments when she puts two and two together. Chastain is remarkably locked-in as the aging country star — a woman who doesn’t want to be seen but is forced back into the spotlight. However, as convincing as her conception of Misty may be, it doesn’t matter all that much when every plot turn seems to fall into her lap.

This passive experience is further marred by mechanical filmmaking. While it all technically coheres — the nighttime spaces, lit by halogen signs, are all appropriately noxious; Feste manages to capture Chastain’s close-ups with clarity — you could practically set your watch by how each subplot plays out, and the way learning something new sends Misty charging to a new location at the end of practically every scene. It’s a languid film with no breathing room, an oxymoron that makes sense once the film winds up and you can recount how much has happened by way of plot, and how little by way of story or emotional development. For instance, there are hints and flashbacks about her ex-husband and musical partner Clark (John Hawkes) throughout, but his appearance is relegated to late in the runtime while his actual role as a specter of her past ends up with little actual impact.

The pieces for some other more rigorous story all appear to be in place, from people Misty knows she can’t trust to former friends with whom she needs to make amends. Unfortunately, Heartland strings these together in rote fashion. Its camera is used to tell more than to show, and its country music interludes play like wheel-spinning interruptions despite gesturing at phantom connections between violence and the genre at large. The film, as a whole, feels episodic and disconnected.

Through it all, Chastain remains remarkable as ever; unfortunately, it’s as a woman who would rather be anywhere else — a feeling that’s hard to shake when sitting down to watch Heartland for yourself.

articles.title: Some of These GTA 6 Clips Look So Good That I Don't Care if It's Running at 30fps
articles.summary: Earlier this week, Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 would be running at 30fps on all of the consoles, including the PS5 Pro. And while I wasn't surprised, I've been watching some of the clips that have been trickling out this week, and I can't say I'm not excited to play it, even at 30fps.
articles.body:
This is an opinion piece by Jackie Thomas, IGN's Senior Tech Editor who has been writing about PC hardware for more than a decade.

Earlier this week, Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 would be running at 30fps on all of the consoles , including the PS5 Pro. And while I wasn't surprised, I've been watching some of the clips that have been trickling out this week, and I can't say I'm not excited to play it, even at 30fps.

The one that really got my attention is this one from Instagram account onlyindade. It's a simple clip of some cars slowly driving down the road, but it looks downright incredible. I've been staring at high-end graphics for 20 years, and even I had to do a double take to make sure it wasn't just real-life footage. The footage is highly compressed and it's hard to make out some of the details, but even with compression artifacts, you can tell GTA 6 is going to be an absolutely stunning game.

Pausing the video and looking at the road, the texture quality is incredible. You can make out individual bumps in the asphalt, along with little pieces of debris on the side of the road. Looking at the cars themselves, the reflections in the cars' paint are beautiful and make it look like an actual material. The shadows, too, are nice and soft and behave similarly to how you'd expect the actual shadows of the cars to behave, leaning away from where the sun is.

These clips from onlyindade don't specify which platform they were captured on, but I'd put my money on the PS5 Pro . In its blog earlier this week , Rockstar said the PS5 Pro would have PSSR upscaling and ray traced shadows that are exclusive to that console. Looking at the shadows cast by the cars in that clip, along with the lack of aliasing on the distant buildings – which admittedly might be drowned out by compression blurriness – it definitely looks like PSSR helped quite a bit.

Onlyindade shared another clip , this time with the camera inside of a car and looking out the window as it drives down the street. Just like in the first clip, the textures on the car door are pristine, and just straight-up look real. Later on in the clip, when whoever's behind the camera is walking on the sidewalk, the camera looks at a blue and pink car that looks like it came straight out of the '50s.

In that part of the scene, it's not the car that impresses me, but rather the shadows cast from the palm tree above it. Again, this clip is super compressed, but you can make out individual leaves in the shadows. There's also a character standing next to the car on his phone, and the shadows there look phenomenal and even move flawlessly as he does.

When looking at these clips, it's important to keep in mind that both the PS5 and the Xbox Series X are running on graphics architectures that are going on 7 years old at this point. It doesn't help that those graphics chips are paired with CPUs that are just as old. Even with that aging hardware, it sure seems like Rockstar was able to craft something that looks better than any other game on the market right now.

Maybe it was just my internet connection, but all of the clips shared by that Dade County Instagram account are extremely compressed, and so it's very possible that some red flags were grayed out. In a huge open world like this with long draw distances, the detail on distant objects is usually the first thing to fall, especially as the game runs out of VRAM budget.

In that first clip, it looks like the edges of distant objects are going to be crisp, but the compression artifacts make those kinds of details seem wobbly no matter how good they look. There's a decent chance that when I boot this game up on my PS5 Pro at launch, I'm going to be assaulted by jagged edges on distant streetlights and buildings – and that is one of my pet peeves. But it doesn't look like that's the case. I just hope I haven't been fooled by online compression.

More than anything, these clips confirm that 60fps was probably out of the question for the current-generation consoles. With this level of fidelity, I'm just surprised it's running at all. But the one thought that keeps bouncing around in my head is, "Just how good will this look when I can run it on an RTX 5090 and a 9800X3D ?" Now I just have to sit and wait for Rockstar to port the game. Hopefully the rumors about the PC port coming out next year are true.

articles.title: Peace Disturbed - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Peace Disturbed is a fairly classic Side Quest in The Witcher 3, as it sends Geralt off into a dark, dingy cave -- or in this particular instance, a crypt --
articles.body:
Peace Disturbed is a fairly classic Side Quest in The Witcher 3, as it sends Geralt off into a dark, dingy cave -- or in this particular instance, a crypt -- tasking him with defeating a barrage of different creatures to help out local townsfolk.

To help you make it through the crypt unscathed and find the Daystar Steel Sword, here's IGN's complete guide to Peace Disturbed, including every key character location.

To start Peace Disturbed, you'll need to head to Ard Skellig, looking in the south for a crypt. Outside the crypt, there'll be two women who act as the quest-givers here.

The duo will describe the crypt as haunted, saying Geralt needs to head in and remove nails from the corpses inside, to prevent Wraiths from using the nails to build longships. Sounds like a fun story, but sure -- head on in to the crypt and get ready to tangle with some Wraiths.

It's a linear crypt -- almost like a mini-dungeon -- and it'll be largely populated by level 24 Wraiths. Where possible, try to take them on one at a time, using Yrden and Igni, along with weapons soaked with Specter Oil.

At the very end of the crypt, you'll be able to find a Nightwraith, which is level 25. This is slightly tankier Wraith, essentially, but the same weaknesses -- Yrden for tangible physical forms and Specter Oil for heavier damage -- will still help to cut it down.

Remember to loot the Wraiths on your way out once the area has been cleared. There's also a Daystar Steel Sword tucked away in the crypt, so make sure to grab that before leaving.

Return to the pair of women outside the crypt to finish the Side Quest.

You'll get 50 x experience for completing this Side Quest.

articles.title: Barbie Rewind Review - IGN
articles.body:
Barbie Rewind feels like the equivalent of showing your children the family heirloom rocking horse, and then watching them poke it and ask if they can play Roblox. A weird mix of nostalgia and interior decorating sim, it's home to 17 retro Barbie games and a dreamhouse to arrange Barbie-appropriate furniture in. Now, it's been over three decades since I last smashed a Barbie against a G.I. Joe and made smooching noises, so I called in two gaming experts, Kora (9) and Paloma (5), to assist with this review. Sadly, unlike her looks, time has not been kind to Barbie's gaming legacy.

"That doesn't make sense. Why does she have a scuba mask but not a toilet?" A crucial question from Kora as the girls got stuck into the only bit of Barbie Rewind they actually cared about: the decorating. This might be selling itself as a collection of Barbie games from 1991's NES Barbie through to 2007's Barbie as the Island Princess, but its newly created Dreamhouse mode is the big winner here. There are more than 250 pieces of furniture, and some of them are unlocked by playing the retro Barbie games. The big B and other characters like Ken and Christie give you quests, but they're just to decorate the house, so it's a bit like someone saying "be careful" when you're already falling down the stairs.

The Barbie games themselves got what I would call a polite fiddle. I played all of them before the expert advisors were called in, and Rewind is heavy on minigames of the platforming and "catch the falling coconut" variety. These games haven't been given the Monkey Island-style reboot; they're presented seemingly entirely as is, but with a frame that relates to their various consoles to help smooth over any aspect ratio issues.

It's great as a museum piece, but show it to anyone born after 2010 and they basically look like cave paintings. "Is that meant to be Barbie?" asks Kora incredulously, squinting at Barbie Pet Rescue. Paloma picks up the controller to play one of the minigames, a sort of cat Pong using two paws that is apparently essential to pet care, and watches the ball of yarn awkwardly bounce off the screen. She knows controllers, she plays Lego Batman, but this minigame makes no sense. The ball is slow, the angles are off, and Paloma looks at me exasperated as if I personally offended her.

Controls were an issue throughout, changing between games in a way that meant looking up the button layout for everything they wanted to try. One smart addition is the option to tweak things like your total health in certain games, which makes for a less stressful experience all round. The girls liked the concept of a lot of them – veterinarian duties, horse racing, and the fashion dress-up doll in particular – but these are kids born long after the time when you knew that what you saw on the cover of a game was light years away from how it actually looked. I could burn through pixelated bouncing and stilted dialogue on nostalgia alone, but Kora and Paloma are playing Hogwarts Legacy; they have iPad games, and their eyes know not the trauma of staring into a Gameboy Color in the back of a moving vehicle.

articles.title: Grow Room Guide: How to Set Up and Make Money - Rob Run Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Grow Room is an available expansion that you can add to your home in Rob Run. It's a way for you to make passive money while you're playing, but
articles.body:
The Grow Room is an available expansion that you can add to your home in Rob Run . It's a way for you to make passive money while you're playing, but it does require a few steps before you can set it up. In this guide, we're going to share with you the best way to set it up and how you can use it to make money while playing Rob Run.

You can purchase the Grow Room from the Black Market. You first need to purchase the deed for the Grow Room and spend $150,000 to unlock it. You also need access to a level 1 Settlement house if you want to place it down.

With the Grow Room set up, there's still one more thing you need to buy from the Black Market: a Grow Table. The Grow Table is where you can keep your plants. You can buy the blueprint from the Black Market for $40,000, and then it costs $30,000 to get one, for a total of $70,000. Bring the purchased blueprint down to your Grow Room and place it down at one of the available locations.

With the Grow Room set down, and the Grow Table ready to go, the last thing you need is the Growing Planet. You have the chance to acquire these plants by participating in heists throughout Looty Bay. These plants randomly spawn behind shops, and you'll need to be a Criminal to pick them up.

These are considered Cargo, which means you can't place them in your inventory. Instead, you have to pick them up, haul them to your vehicle, and place them in your trunk. You typically find one at these locations, so the standard starting vehicle should be sufficient for you to race out of the map, and return home.

Now, the way you make money with your Grow Room all comes down to the plants. The plants have a harvest period, typically taking an hour to reach its full height. You can increase this by using various items, such as water pumps, fans, and growing lamps. These gradually increase the speed of how long it takes for a Grow Plant to become harvestable.

Your plant does not disappear after harvesting it. The plant remains here. It's not going to disappear. Instead, you'll get a small bag of the contents from the Grow Plant, and you can take that to Looty Bay and sell it to a Fence. The item works like standard items you sell to a Fence, which means there's a risk of other players (or Cops ) taking it from you if they encounter you first.

You'll be able to repeat this rotation as many times as you want, gradually adding more Grow Plants to your Grow Table and acquiring bags from it to sell in Looty Bay.

articles.title: How to Defeat Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet is likely to be the first boss you come across in Phantom Blade Zero. But, you aren't meant to beat her at the beginning
articles.body:
The Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet is likely to be the first boss you come across in Phantom Blade Zero . But, you aren't meant to beat her at the beginning of the game. She is a part of the Triple Threat tale.

She is a deadly threat this early on and will likely overwhelm you, but compared to most of the other bosses in the game, she is not a complex fight, just a long one (depending on your weapon level. Ideally, you want to come back to her once you reach Pangzhen, the fourth area in the game.

How to Defeat Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet

The main tactic with her is to block and parry as many of her attacks as you can. She doesn't have many complex attacks, and although she teleports a lot, once you learn the attack timings, the majority of her attacks become less intimidating.

There aren't any specific weapons or Phantom Edges that help in this fight particularly, as you will be parrying for the most part. But, generally, some of the best weapons work well, like the White Serpent and Crimson Viper . You want your main weapon to be around level 10-15, to ensure you are able to do enough damage.

Occasionally, she can leave a longer pause, but the vertical portal is usually used mid-combo.

Every hit can be parried, bar the grab at the end of the combo, which must be dodged.

As mentioned, this is a parry-fight. You want to learn the parry timing of the puppet, and parry as many attacks as possible to weaken her Sha-Chi meter. When that occurs you can overwhelm her with attacks, Phantom Edges and special attacks.

This fight will still take a while due to her health bar, around 4-6 minutes depending on your weapon level. But, it is not a complex fight at all, compared to much of what you have already faced at this point in the game.

Upon defeating the boss, you will get the Three-Headed Doll, a key story item for this quest.

articles.title: Kevin Feige Didn't Want Wanda in VisionQuest Because He Was Worried She Would 'Distract' From the Core Show
articles.summary: Marvel actor Paul Bettany has said Kevin Feige didn't want Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff to be in VisionQuest because he was worried she might "distract" from the show's core.
articles.body:
Marvel actor Paul Bettany has said Kevin Feige didn't want Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff to be in VisionQuest because he was worried she might "distract" from the show's core.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe star recalled the conversation he had with the Marvel Studios bigwig when speaking with The Playlist . MCU followers spent the months leading up to the new Disney+ offshoot speculating about how it may serve as a vehicle for an unlikely resurrection.

Those who have kept up with the nearly 20-year-old cinematic universe will remember that Wanda met her end in the closing moments of 2022's Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness . She's yet to be seen since, and although discussions about seeing her share a screen with Vision were had, Bettany said it was an idea Feige was never too fond of.

"There were questions about it, whether that should happen, whether it opened up too much for the MCU, whether they wanted to do it later," he remembered. "I don't know. But I remember having this conversation with [Kevin], and he said, 'You and Terry have done such a great job at making me care about Vision. I really don’t think you should distract from that by giving the audience that at the end of the [show].

"It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own.' And I think he was right."

The main events of VisionQuest came and went without any signs that Olsen had recorded new footage to fit directly within VisionQuest, leaving the MCU without a proper family reunion. It was a disappointing moment for those who had spent months speculating she would reappear ahead of Avengers: Doomsday as theories were finally put to rest .

Warning! Spoilers for VisionQuest's finale credits scenes follow.

If you've finished VisionQuest, you'll know that disappointment didn't last long. Just as the final credits for the finale episode came to an end, viewers were taken back to Wanda's resting place on the snowy cliffs of Mount Wundagore. There, a cloaked figure that looks and sounds a lot like Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom reaches out to her, saying, "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." Then, her eyes open.

Yes, Olsen and Wanda Maximoff are coming back, with the return set up alongside VisionQuest's finale, despite Feige's wishes. To be fair, the reveal mostly seemed to consist of reused footage from her appearance in the Doctor Strange sequel. The scene is also just about as far removed from VisionQuest itself as it can be. So, while Feige may have wanted to avoid Wanda distracting from the partial family reunion we got in VisionQuest, her inclusion at least managed to arrive long after the main story wrapped up.

We'll hopefully know more about Wanda's future – and hopefully whether or not she'll reunite with Vision, Billy, and Tommy – when Avengers: Doomsday premieres next month , December 18. Until then, you can check out what IGN thought of VisionQuest's finale in our 7/10 review .

"The last-minute addition of a new villain derails the finale of VisionQuest somewhat," we said, "but the series still succeeds where Vision and Ultron are concerned."

articles.title: Before Directing the Biggest Success of His Career, Steven Spielberg Almost Made an Alien Horror Movie Instead
articles.summary: Before directing E.T., Steven Spielberg almost made an alien horror movie called Night Skies.
articles.body:
In the late 1970s/early 1980s, Steven Spielberg was developing a movie that ultimately would never get made. And yet, from a different perspective, it actually would get made… as a bunch of other, quite famous films. We’re talking Gremlins. We’re talking Poltergeist. And we’re talking E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial .

“It was a dream team of people working on this thing. It was going to be a horror movie about these evil aliens, or mischievous aliens, that come to this rural farmstead and really mess with this family – they really fuck with this family,” explains movie journalist and author Max Evry, who just released a book about the film called Stranded on Earth: How Night Skies Became E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial .

Dream team is putting it lightly, as Night Skies had Spielberg producing, John Sayles scripting, production illustrator Ron Cobb expected to make his directorial debut, and Rick Baker designing the aliens. And of course, Kathleen Kennedy was also onboard, as she was working for Spielberg at this point in her career and would soon get her first full producer credit on E.T.

I recently spoke to Evry, who is also an occasional contributor to IGN – and who you may recall was also the author of that very popular book about David Lynch’s Dune, A Masterpiece in Disarray , from a couple of years back. We discussed how Night Skies went from alien horror movie to the family-friendly mega-hit that was E.T., how Poltergeist and Gremlins were born alongside its development, and how Stranded on Earth is, as the author puts it, “a hard R-rated book about a children's movie.”

From Close Encounters to a ‘Famous Clusterfuck’... to E.T.

Stranded on Earth begins with a look back at Spielberg’s earliest filmmaking endeavors as a teen, including a film called Firelight which he made for $500 and which actually got a theatrical release – in the wunderkind’s hometown for one night, at least (the director’s semi-autobiographical film The Fabelmans recreates this moment from his life). The film was an early example of Spielberg’s interest in UFOs and the creatures behind them.

“We're dealing with Spielberg, we're dealing with aliens, so we got to go all the way back to when he was 15, 16, making his first sort of feature film,” says Evry. “It was like this two-hour epic that he made when he was a teenager, and that story is really fun. It sets up the way that Spielberg deals with aliens throughout his career, because it's like Martin Scorsese and gangsters. Spielberg has used aliens as a vessel for whatever kind of creative mood he happens to be in. I don't believe – and there are many people who corroborate this in the book – he has a firm belief one way or the other about alien visitations and things like that. I think it's just a great tool that he uses to explore different subjects.”

Of course, Spielberg would have great success with 1977’s Close Encounters of the Third Kind , and the book recounts the filmmaker’s less than enthusiastic plans for a direct sequel to that film. That’s where Night Skies comes into the picture.

“They spent close to a million dollars developing this thing. Some people in the book described it as kind of a weird science experiment, like maybe it'll go, maybe it won't. But it was heavily developed, and I think would've been a great movie,” says Evry.

This was all going on during a very memorable time for Spielberg, because he also had the infamous misfire 1941 , a World War II-era comedy starring an ensemble that included John Belushi, hit theaters in 1979. As Evry puts it, the film was “a famous clusterfuck … a nightmare production where he was essentially going crazy with this thing, and it just kept getting bigger and bigger and bigger. … It hurt his reputation a lot, and it sort of showed he wasn't bulletproof.”

The fallout from 1941 would impact how Night Skies – and then as it morphed into what would become E.T. – was viewed by the studios.

“There were a lot of people who thought he might be done,” he says. “So even after this project evolved from Night Skies to E.T., it became almost like this nuclear football where Columbia had it and then they just decided they didn't want it and they gave it to Universal. Universal was kind of like, ‘Eh. We'll do it, but you have to raise the money through a bond company. We don't want to directly fund it because we don't want to be responsible if you go over budget again.’ It was this interesting period where it was like the last time people didn't trust Steven Spielberg.”

Evolution of an Idea, From Aliens to Ghosts to Gremlins

Spielberg was never going to direct Night Skies, and in fact it was during this period that he began to produce other directors’ films, the earliest examples being Robert Zemeckis’ I Wanna Hold Your Hand (1978) and Used Cars (1980). Zemeckis, with his partner Bob Gale, also worked on a script for Spielberg at one point called After School, “and that had a lot of elements that carried forward into E.T. also,” says Evry. “So it's not just Night Skies. It was sort of [Spielberg] blending After School with Night Skies, and that's how you get E.T.”

But before that, when Night Skies was still Night Skies, it was Ron Cobb who was going to direct the film.

“It was going to be his debut, and he developed it from the ground up,” says Evry. “There's some false information out there that it was between Cobb and Tobe Hooper. That is not true. Basically, Tobe Hooper came in much later when Cobb was ensconced in Spain doing the production design for Conan the Barbarian, and he couldn't come back and work on Night Skies. Rick Baker's doing storyboards for the film without him. I think at that point, Spielberg calls up Tobe Hooper and is like, ‘Hey, I've got this alien project. Are you interested in directing it?’ Tobe Hooper was like, ‘Nah, but I'd like to do a movie about ghosts.’”

And of course, that project became Poltergeist . Evry explains that while many film fans think that Night Skies fed into Poltergeist, the two projects were really in parallel development.

“They were happening at the exact same time, and that's interesting because they're both about essentially these families with the same makeup, like mom, dad, three kids, one older, one younger, one very young,” he says. “And the focal point is on the youngest one, and you've got this supernatural force encroaching upon their house. In one case, it's ghosts. In one case, it's aliens.”

There are even some lines from the Night Skies scripts which can be found in Poltergeist – “They’re here…” for example.

In Evry’s view, Gremlins has a lot more of Night Skies in it though. While Gremlins originated as a spec script by Chris Columbus, John Sayles took over as a ghost writer after Columbus. And Sayles was also the main writer behind Night Skies.

“So that is where you start to see some crossover and some of the similar ideas,” says Evry. “I mean, even down to the fact that Night Skies was inspired by this ‘real incident’ called the Kelly-Hopkinsville Incident of 1955, which was aliens attacking a farm. It's a famous thing in UFO-logy, and there's a whole chapter about it in the book.” (Evry even visited Hopkinsville for his research.)

That’s where the term “little green men” comes from, and as Evry points out, at the end of Gremlins they refer to the little creatures as little green men.

“If you look at the actual eyewitness drawings of the aliens from Kelly-Hopkinsville, they look a hell of a lot like the Gremlins,” adds the author.

For Evry, the key creative force behind Night Skies that he wanted to talk to was legendary makeup effects creator Rick Baker. But for Baker, this was a project that elicited a lot of painful memories.

“In some ways, he's the central figure and it's the most dramatic element of the book,” says Evry. “John Sayles and Ron Cobb, they both came out of it just fine. But for Rick, it was a really tough experience, which we talk about – for whatever reason, he and Spielberg just had this tremendous falling out, very dramatic. And it was a trauma for him. And it's like, I never wanted to portray seven-time Oscar winner Rick Baker as some kind of victim, but the thing you have to remember is at that time he was zero-Oscar winner Rick Baker. He was still kind of new to the business.”

It seems Spielberg has his own take on what went down between him and Baker on Night Skies, and it doesn’t necessarily match with how Baker remembers it.

“There's another book about E.T. where Spielberg – I didn't put this in my book because I thought it was embarrassing – his quote was, ‘Rick and I decided this was not the project we were going to work on,’” says Evry. “If you read [my] book, you'll have a different feeling about that quote. But Rick, he was very honest and he was very candid, which was so great to hear him talk about it. And I talked to other people who were in his studio as well, and they corroborate everything he says.”

Baker was actually working on An American Werewolf in London at the same time that he was on Night Skies, and of course that film would go on to be an incredible breakthrough success in large part due to Baker’s effects work.

“An important thing to note is you've seen American Werewolf, and you know how innovative that was,” says Evry. “And I am here to tell you that his work on Night Skies was just as good, if not better. I actually discovered the original VHS Night Skies alien test that he did that he sent to Spielberg, and it's unbelievable. If you did it today, it would still stand up. And this is far and away ahead of anything being done in makeup effects in 1980. The alien was so expressive, so versatile. It was really cool. It was really eerie.” (You can check out a glimpse of it here .)

Of course, that’s the trick with any history lesson – whose memories are correct, who has embellished a story, knowingly or not, and where does what really happened come to the forefront? Evry says that’s part of the fun of his book, as it gets into a sort of “Rashomon, where there's a chapter on John Sayles, there's a chapter on Ron Cobb, there's a chapter on Rick Baker, and you start to see the story from different angles.”

Of course, one undeniable aspect to it all is that at some point, Spielberg decided to make E.T. instead.

“Spielberg has this intuitive creativity where he just said, ‘You know what? I think I can do something else with this,’” says Evry. “I'm really excited for horror fans, science fiction fans, but especially Spielberg fans to come away from this book with just a totally different perspective on what E.T. is, on what it could have been, and on what came after.”
